newsitem.title: USA: SunRiver sells unit to Cyberguard.
newsitem.headline: SunRiver sells unit to Cyberguard.

text.p: Network computer maker SunRiver Corp said Thursday it had sold "substantially all" of the assets of a software unit to CyberGuard Corp in a deal worth $350,000.
SunRiver said it sold the assets of TradeWave Corp for a combination of cash, royalty on certain future revenues and assumption of selected liabilities by CyberGuard.
"The total aggregate amount being paid is not expected to be material to SunRiver Corp," it said, adding that the deal closed Wednesday.
SunRiver said TradeWave developed Internet software and value-added services that enable private, secure communications and electronic commerce transactions over the Internet.
CyberGuard develops intranet/Internet security software for companies.

SunRiver said it had discontinued TradeWave's operations and taken a one-time, after-tax charge in the fourth quarter of 1996. "The sale, therefore, is not expected to have a material impact on the company's second quarter ending June 30," it said.
